label: origin_1978_oho
event: SSA Office of Hearings and Appeals administrative standardization of ALJ hearing procedures via HALLEX
date: circa 1978-1980 — post-Mathews v. Eldridge (1976); exact HALLEX publication dates in OHO transmittals

sources.description: Supreme Court decision establishing due process framework for disability benefit procedures; prompted SSA to codify procedural minimums
Statutory requirement for written findings and decisions after ALJ hearings
ALJ hearing procedure regulations — regulatory framework HALLEX implements
ALJ hearing procedures — notice, opening, testimony, expert witness examination
Closing the record — post-hearing submissions, decision timing requirements
Social Security Ruling — VE testimony consistency with DOT requirement; operationalized in HALLEX

significance: HALLEX converted ALJ hearing procedures from discretionary practices into enforceable procedural rights. Courts treat HALLEX violations that prejudice claimants as reversible error. The VE hypothetical completeness rule and written decision requirements are among the most frequently litigated HALLEX provisions.
